The problem

Token leaderboards reward spending, not shipping, and most teams that ran them dropped them.

What it does

Bloodrank ranks people who run AI coding agents on what they spend and what they actually ship, side by side.

How it works

  1. Blood: monthly AI spend, log-scaled so a big budget cannot buy the top
  2. Kills: deploys, launches and revenue, verified through GitHub and payment records
  3. A Sunlight board for days fully offline

The public board is planned to be free.

Stop guessing whether your agent spend is paying off.

TodayThe site is live with sample data, labelled as such. The service, the board and `npx bloodrank` are not built.

Aims

Autonomous operation
The boards keep themselves: spend and shipped work are read from the tools and from GitHub and payment records, scored, ranked and published every night without anyone entering numbers.
Intelligence
Plain scoring code, log-scaled and published. A model only helps check that a claimed kill (a deploy, a launch, revenue) is real before it counts.
Growth
Community-led: builders share their coffin cards. Growth is verified profiles on the public board, counted from the first one that is not ours.
The technical detail

A leaderboard for AI vampires: builders who run several AI coding agents at once. Each profile gets a Vampire Score from 0 to 1000: 40% blood (monthly AI spend, log-scaled), 40% kills (deploys, launches, merged features and revenue, verified through GitHub and payment records) and 20% night (parallel agents and late-night usage), with ranks from Thrall to Count. A Sunlight board counts days fully offline, because the essay that coined the term was about burnout. What exists today is the concept site with sample data; the service is not built.
